components.html:
ChromaScope

A simple CLI to get a visual diff across various browser engines

PlaywrightCLI
components.css: .ds-planet-card { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 32px; padding: 32px 16px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--color-foreground); text-decoration: none; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; backdrop-filter: blur(16px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-foreground) 10%, transparent); background-image: linear-gradient(to bottom right, rgb(255 255 255 / 0), transparent); transition: background-image 300ms; } .ds-planet-card:hover { background-image: linear-gradient(to bottom right, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.05), transparent); } .ds-planet-card:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-background), 0 0 0 4px var(--color-primary); } .ds-planet { position: relative; width: 160px; height: 160px; margin: 0 auto; } .ds-planet-body { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, #6b8fb8, #1e3a5f 70%); filter: grayscale(1) brightness(0.9) contrast(1.1) saturate(0.9); transition: transform 300ms, filter 300ms; } .ds-planet-card:hover .ds-planet-body { transform: scale(1.05); filter: grayscale(0) brightness(0.9) contrast(1.1) saturate(0.9); } .ds-planet-ring { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; outline: 2px dashed transparent; transition: inset 300ms 300ms, outline-color 300ms 300ms; } .ds-planet-card:hover .ds-planet-ring { inset: -16px; outline-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-foreground) 10%, transparent); } .ds-planet-orbit { position: absolute; inset: -16px; border-radius: 9999px; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 300ms 600ms; animation: ds-orbit 24s linear infinite; } .ds-planet-card:hover .ds-planet-orbit { opacity: 1; } .ds-planet-moon { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 0; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 9999px; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); background: radial-gradient(at 25% 25%, var(--color-accent), rgb(245 158 11 / 0.8) 75%); } @keyframes ds-orbit { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } .ds-planet-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 400; text-align: center; } .ds-planet-desc { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.43; text-align: center; } .ds-planet-tags { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a navigator's chart of a small universe. A clean, dark sci-fi base (near-black space, faint drifting stars, two half-lit planets on the horizon) carries the structure, and a handwritten voice scribbles notes in the margins: the Caveat wordmark, the wavy gold underline, the odd emphasised word. The chart is precise; the handwriting is what makes it one person's chart.

It should feel curious, handmade and nerdy. Curious: projects are bodies to approach, and each one rewards a closer look. Handmade: a little imperfect, a little playful, clearly not a template. Nerdy: sci-fi references and nods to the retro web are welcome, as long as they stay legible. Interactive pieces are minimal and restrained; most of the screen is calm, and the energy comes from small, exact details.

It must never drift toward neon cyberpunk (heavy glows, glitch effects, saturated neon everywhere) or corporate SaaS (gradient heroes, stock illustration, generic feature-card grids).
keyCharacteristics: Near-black space with a sparse, slowly drifting starfield behind everything.
One sans family (Lato) for structure; Caveat handwriting only for the wordmark and short accents.
Two signal colors used sparingly: Plasma Magenta for interaction, Comet Yellow for handwritten emphasis.
Depth from light, blur and glow; no drop shadows on UI.
Projects shown as planets: circular, greyscale at rest, coming into color when approached.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Magenta means "you can interact with this"; yellow means "this is the handwritten voice". Don't swap them, and don't introduce a third signal color for UI.

rules.name: The Dark Sky Rule
rules.body: Signal colors appear as lines, rings and outlines, never as large filled areas. If a screen has a magenta or yellow block bigger than a tag, it has drifted toward neon.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: Caveat is for the wordmark and short inline accents of one to three words. Never set a paragraph, heading or UI label in it.

rules.name: The Starlight Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand out, give it light (a glow, a rim, a lift in brightness), not a drop shadow. Glows stay faint, at 10% opacity or less, so they never read as neon.

dos: Do keep the background near-black (`oklch(18.98% 0 294)`) with the starfield and planets fixed behind the content.
Do use Plasma Magenta only for interaction (focus, outlines, hover) and Comet Yellow only for handwritten emphasis.
Do keep components quiet at rest and let state changes be subtle and exact (300ms transitions, small scale steps, opacity shifts).
Do build depth with blur, faint rims and glows at 10% opacity or less.
Do keep circles for things that are "bodies" (planets, moons, avatars) and gentle 6–12px corners for containers.
Do use the theme tokens (`foreground`, `background`, `primary`, `accent`) with opacity rather than adding new grey values.
donts: Don't add neon-cyberpunk treatments: strong glows, glitch effects, scanlines or saturated neon fills.
Don't add corporate SaaS patterns: gradient hero banners, stock illustrations, generic icon-and-heading feature grids.
Don't set more than a few words in Caveat, or use it for UI labels.
Don't put drop shadows under cards or buttons.
Don't fill large areas with Plasma Magenta or Comet Yellow.
Don't add a light theme or theme toggle; the site is dark only.
